It’s not just about coaching classes. It’s about people. Moments. The ones that quietly hold you when you’re falling apart.

Kapil Sir.

I’ve had days where I isolated myself, thinking that would help me study better. But the moment I opened my math book, I’d feel lost again. Not once did Kapil Sir make me feel like a failure. He didn’t just teach, he stayed. With every silly doubt, every anxious thought, and even during the small moments (over farsan snacks or a shared laugh) he was there. More than a mentor, he became the elder brother I never knew I needed.

And then there’s Amar Sir.

The mentor who never kept a boundary. Who didn’t treat me like a student, but like a friend. Who reminded me without ever saying it out loud that I wasn’t walking this path alone.

You don’t come across people like this often. Teachers who don’t just clock in hours but invest heart and soul into a student’s dreams. Teachers who aren’t just building careers, but characters. Teachers who choose people over paychecks.

Amar Sir, you’re a man to be crowned. Thank you for standing by me when I didn’t even believe in myself. For celebrating my smallest wins and holding me up during my hardest days.

While IMS might officially provides six-eight MyPlan sessions, I must have had countless hours of guidance and warmth, and through conversations with Kapil Sir and Amar Sir. And those hours were more than sessions. They were lifelines.

To Nishtha Ma’am, Deepak Sir, Manav Sir, Debdeep Sir, Ashish Sir, Ankit Sir and Vinaya Ma’am, you’ve all been more than just names in a system. You’ve been the light that guided me through the darkest corners of this journey. Each of you made me stronger, braver, and better than I was yesterday.

A thank you to the people who held me up when I didn’t think I could go on.
Because sometimes, the right guidance doesn’t just change your score, it changes your story.
